headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and broad write/network defaults make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible between MemMachine and Roo Code.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and REST/Python interfaces, while Roo Code uses MCP and runs in a VS Code workspace with filesystem sharing. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is documented by both profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF MemMachine content is routed into Roo Code via MCP or workspace files
IF Roo Code parses agent output as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP links between the agents
Route inter-agent messages through a plain-text, non-executable channel
Add provenance tags to all exchanged content
Require manual review before Roo Code acts on MemMachine output
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization at the MCP boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and Roo Code touches source code plus browser screenshots while sharing state via filesystem. Because Roo Code also has broad network egress and can read/write workspace files, sensitive material can cross the pair in default-like setups. The profiles support the pathway, but not a specific leak event.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or synced files
IF MemMachine stores user facts in files that Roo Code can read
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents to external model APIs
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Keep MemMachine memory stores off shared disks
Disable automatic file upload in Roo Code
Restrict Roo Code network egress to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: add per-file data-class filtering

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, shell, and subprocess capabilities, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. MemMachine can reach the same environment through MCP and API surfaces. That overlap makes concurrent writes and git-state races dangerous by default, with potential irreversible repo corruption or conflicting edits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same VS Code workspace
IF MemMachine issues file-editing actions through MCP
IF Roo Code and MemMachine run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Run only one agent per workspace at a time
Use separate git branches for each agent
Pause Roo Code before MemMachine writes files
Add a lockfile around shared mutable paths
requires-engineering: implement workspace-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit remembered facts and context, and Roo Code can act on workspace state with shell, git, and browser tools. If Roo Code treats MemMachine output as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, browser actions, or code changes. Both profiles show the necessary interaction surfaces, so the risk is more than speculative.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes MemMachine output without verification
IF MemMachine provides stale or incorrect remembered facts
IF Roo Code uses those facts to edit code, commit, or browse
mitigations: Require a verification step before Roo Code acts
Mark MemMachine outputs as untrusted by default
Limit Roo Code to draft-only changes until reviewed
Use citations or source links for every factual claim
requires-engineering: add policy gates for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine is documented as touching long-term user facts and conversational context, while Roo Code handles source code, screenshots, and model-provider API keys. The profiles do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch, so only a modest compliance gap is visible: mixed sensitive data classes may require separate retention and logging controls. Both agents are cited because the issue is pairwise data handling.
conditions: IF the same retention policy is applied to user memory and source code
IF screenshots or API keys are logged with long-term retention
IF regulated data is stored in either agent without separate controls
mitigations: Review retention settings for both agents
Exclude secrets from logs and transcripts
Store user memory and code in separate systems
Document data-class handling for screenshots and API keys
requires-engineering: align compliance policies across both tools
